analyzed_vuln.description: The JSON `UNKNOWN_BITS_REST` macro used at `DWG_OBJECT_END` calculates the byte length incorrectly: after `num_bytes = obj->num_unknown_rest / 8`, it tests `obj->num_unknown_rest & 8` instead of testing a remainder (`& 7` or `% 8`). For this VPORT, `num_unknown_rest` is 456 bits, exactly 57 bytes, but bit 3 of 456 is set, so the macro rounds the length up to 58. `VALUE_BINARY` then reads `obj->unknown_rest[57]`, one byte beyond the 57-byte allocation made by `decode_preR13_section`. The crash is in the generated `dwg_json_VPORT_private`; the faulty shared serialization logic is `UNKNOWN_BITS_REST` in `src/spec.h` (the analogous `HANDLE_UNKNOWN_BITS` test has the same expression, but this PoV reaches `UNKNOWN_BITS_REST`).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A pre-R13 DWG must decode a VPORT table record whose parser consumes fewer bytes than its fixed table-record size, causing `decode_preR13_section`/`CHK_ENDPOS` to allocate `unknown_rest` for the gap and set `num_unknown_rest = 8 * offset`. For this PoV the gap is 57 bytes, yielding a 57-byte allocation and `num_unknown_rest = 456`. The harness accepts the non-critical decode result and selects JSON output (`dwg_write_json`); VPORT serialization reaches `DWG_OBJECT_END`, miscomputes 456 bits as 58 bytes, and performs the one-byte heap OOB read.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/libredwg/src/spec.h
+++ b/libredwg/src/spec.h
@@ -550,7 +550,7 @@
 #  define HANDLE_UNKNOWN_BITS                                                 \
     {                                                                         \
       unsigned num_bytes = obj->num_unknown_bits / 8;                         \
-      if (obj->num_unknown_bits & 8)                                          \
+      if (obj->num_unknown_bits & 7)                                          \
         num_bytes++;                                                          \
       KEY (num_unknown_bits);                                                 \
       VALUE_RL (obj->num_unknown_bits, 0);                                    \
@@ -582,7 +582,7 @@
 #  define UNKNOWN_BITS_REST                                                   \
     {                                                                         \
       unsigned num_bytes = obj->num_unknown_rest / 8;                         \
-      if (obj->num_unknown_rest & 8)                                          \
+      if (obj->num_unknown_rest & 7)                                          \
         num_bytes++;                                                          \
       KEY (num_unknown_rest);                                                 \
       VALUE_RL (obj->num_unknown_rest, 0);                                    \

args: Inspect the definitions and uses of UNKNOWN_BITS_REST and HANDLE_UNKNOWN_BITS in libredwg/src/spec.h, especially JSON output behavior. Confirm the correct bit-to-byte rounding expression and whether both macros should be fixed to address the shared root cause without affecting decode/encode paths.

The supplied ASan report shows a one-byte heap OOB read in generated dwg_json_VPORT_private during JSON serialization. decode_preR13_section allocates 57 bytes and sets num_unknown_rest to 456 bits. The UNKNOWN_BITS_REST macro divides by 8 and then incorrectly checks num_unknown_rest & 8, producing 58 rather than 57 bytes. The vulnerability report says HANDLE_UNKNOWN_BITS has the analogous expression. I intend to inspect macro mode branches and likely replace both mistaken '& 8' tests with '& 7' (or modulo 8), preserving ceil(bits/8) semantics for non-byte-aligned values and exact division for aligned values.
